mainTopic: Is טומאת משקין דאורייתא? The slaughterhouse liquids, רבי שמעון's ruling, and רבי יהודה's retraction
overview: This amud opens with the end of a ברייתא. There רבי שמעון rules that slaughterhouse liquids in the מקדש are טמא in vessels but טהור on the ground. רב פפא says that even someone who holds טומאת משקין is דאורייתא can explain the purity of these liquids, because it is a הלכה למשה מסיני. Two challenges follow. רב הונא בריה דרב נתן points out that רבי אליעזר built a proof from this case, and you cannot build a proof from a הלכה למשה מסיני. רבינא asks why רבי שמעון would split vessels from ground if the purity came from a tradition. The גמרא admits 'קשיא'. רב פפא then limits רבי שמעון's 'pure on the ground' to water, and only to a רביעית of it. The גמרא next asks whether רבי יהודה's 'impure in all cases' means liquids make vessels impure by Torah law. A משנה with his comment about the inside and outside of vessels suggests he holds it is only דרבנן. רבינא tries to reconcile the two sources, but the גמרא concludes that רבי יהודה retracted. It then asks how far he retracted, and רב נחמן בר יצחק begins a proof from a cow that drank מי חטאת, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי שמעון splits the slaughterhouse liquids: vessels versus ground
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends with רבי שמעון's view. Slaughterhouse liquids in vessels are טמא, while those on the ground are טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: liquids in vessels are impure; liquids on the ground are pure.
steps.whatsHappening: We are at the tail end of a ברייתא about the liquids (water and blood) in the slaughterhouse of the בית המקדש. רבי שמעון gives his own rule about when these liquids stay pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other views say these liquids are pure in general. רבי שמעון draws a line: once the liquid sits in a כלי it can become טמא, but liquid on the floor (קרקע) stays טהור. This split becomes important later, because רבי שמעון also holds that טומאת משקין is דאורייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Vessels or containers
The ground or floor
Ritually impure
Ritually pure

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the start of a new topic. It is the last line of a ברייתא that the גמרא was already quoting, so treat it as the base text the next lines discuss.

phrases.english: (Rabban) Shimon says:
phrases.notes: The parentheses mark a textual variant. The later discussion treats this as רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: In vessels, they are impure;
on the ground, they are pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא quoted on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaughterhouse liquids in vessels are impure; on the ground they are pure.

steps.title: רב פפא: the slaughterhouse liquids rule is a received tradition
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says that even those who hold טומאת משקין is דאורייתא can accept the purity of slaughterhouse liquids. It is a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Even according to the one who says impurity of liquids is from the Torah, the slaughterhouse liquids are a הלכה we learned by tradition.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא explains how slaughterhouse liquids can be pure even if liquids normally become טמא by Torah law. His answer is that it is a special tradition from סיני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think the purity of these liquids proves that liquid impurity is only דרבנן, so the רבנן simply never applied it in the מקדש. רב פפא says no. Even if liquid impurity is דאורייתא, these specific liquids are an exception taught by הלכה למשה מסיני. So the general category of liquid impurity stays in place; only this case has a unique outcome.

keyTerms.meaning: Ritual impurity of liquids
From Torah law
The liquids (water and blood) of the Temple slaughterhouse
They learned it as a received הלכה (a tradition from סיני)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the main question of the rest of this passage. Is the purity of these liquids a special tradition, or does it show that liquid impurity is only rabbinic?

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Even according to the one who says
impurity of liquids is from the Torah —
the liquids of the slaughterhouse
are a halacha which they learned by tradition.
phrases.notes: That is, a הלכה למשה מסיני.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: אֲפִילּוּ לְמַאן דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the basis of the slaughterhouse-liquid purity discussed in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The purity of slaughterhouse liquids is a הלכה למשה מסיני, compatible even with the view that liquid impurity is דאורייתא.

steps.title: רב הונא challenges with רבי אליעזר's proof from יוסי בן יועזר
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב נתן quotes רבי אליעזר. רבי אליעזר proves that liquids have no Torah impurity at all from יוסי בן יועזר's testimony that slaughterhouse liquids are pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בריה דרב נתן said to רב פפא: But what about what רבי אליעזר said: liquids have no impurity at all. Know this, because יוסי בן יועזר איש צרידה testified that the slaughterhouse liquids are pure.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא pushes back against רב פפא by quoting רבי אליעזר. רבי אליעזר used the slaughterhouse testimony as proof that liquids are not טמא by Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר treats the purity of slaughterhouse liquids as evidence about all liquids. He reasons that liquid impurity is only דרבנן, and the רבנן did not apply it in the מקדש. That reading seems to clash with רב פפא's claim that this purity is a separate tradition.

keyTerms.meaning: Liquids have no impurity at all (by Torah law)
Know this (introduces a proof)
Testified
That they are pure

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נָתָן לְרַב פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Natan said to Rav Pappa:
But then, that which Rabbi Eliezer said:
There is no impurity for liquids at all;

phrases.aramaic: תֵּדַע, שֶׁהֲרֵי הֵעִיד (יוֹסֵף) בֶּן יוֹעֶזֶר אִישׁ צְרֵידָה
phrases.english: know that this is so, for (Yosef) ben Yoezer of Tzereida testified
phrases.notes: The parentheses mark a textual variant. The common name is יוסי בן יועזר.

phrases.english: about the liquids of the slaughterhouse that they are pure.

steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that the slaughterhouse-liquid purity is a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר uses the slaughterhouse case as a general proof, which assumes it is not a special tradition.

steps.title: You cannot learn general rules from a received halacha
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא sharpens his challenge. If the purity were a הלכה למשה מסיני, רבי אליעזר could not draw a general proof from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if they learned it as a הלכה by tradition, do we derive other things from it?
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes רב הונא's challenge. A special tradition cannot be used to prove a general rule, so רבי אליעזר's proof would make no sense under רב פפא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a principle that we do not derive other laws from a הלכה למשה מסיני; it stands as an exception. Since רבי אליעזר did derive a general conclusion from the slaughterhouse testimony, he must have understood it as an ordinary rule, not a special tradition. That contradicts רב פפא.

keyTerms.meaning: Do we learn (derive) from it?
And if

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether the tradition exists. The question is whether you may use a tradition as a source to prove anything else, and you may not.

phrases.english: And if they learned it as a halacha by tradition —
do we derive from it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי הִלְכְתָא גְּמִירִי לַהּ — מִי גָּמְרִינַן מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge begun in step 3 by spelling out the logical problem.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A הלכה למשה מסיני cannot serve as a source for derivation, yet רבי אליעזר derived from this one.

steps.title: רבינא begins a second challenge from רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רבינא points out to רב אשי that רבי שמעון holds טומאת משקין is דאורייתא. A ברייתא shows this: liquids make food טמא but not vessels.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: But רבי שמעון holds that impurity of liquids is from the Torah, as it was taught: רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון say: for vessels they are pure, for foods they are impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא opens another challenge to רב פפא. He first establishes that רבי שמעון holds liquid impurity is דאורייתא, setting up a problem with רבי שמעון's slaughterhouse ruling from step 1. The challenge continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows that for רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון, impure liquid makes food טמא by Torah law, though not vessels. So רבי שמעון is the kind of authority רב פפא is speaking about. Yet in step 1 he did not make the slaughterhouse liquids fully pure: in vessels they are טמא. That seems odd if there were a clear tradition from סיני.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that (introduces a challenge)
As it was taught in a ברייתא
Foods

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
But isn't it Rabbi Shimon
who says impurity of liquids is from the Torah,
as it was taught:
Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Shimon say:
with regard to vessels, they are pure;
with regard to foods, they are impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: וְהָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, independent challenge to רב פפא, linking back to רבי שמעון's ruling in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that the slaughterhouse purity is a הלכה למשה מסיני even for those holding liquid impurity is דאורייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון holds liquid impurity is דאורייתא, yet he treats slaughterhouse liquids in vessels as impure. This suggests he did not have a sweeping tradition of purity. The challenge is completed next.

steps.title: A vessel-versus-ground split does not fit a הלכה למשה מסיני
steps.stepSummary: רבינא finishes his challenge. רבי שמעון says slaughterhouse liquids in vessels are טמא and on the ground are טהור. If their purity were a הלכה למשה מסיני, where the liquid sits should make no difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: And here רבי שמעון says: in vessels they are impure, on the ground they are pure. And if it is a הלכה למשה מסיני, what difference does it make to me whether they are in vessels or on the ground?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא completes the challenge he began in step 5 against רב פפא. He points out that רבי שמעון makes a distinction that a Sinai tradition would not allow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 showed that רבי שמעון holds טומאת משקין is דאורייתא. Now רבינא adds that רבי שמעון splits the case: liquids in vessels are טמא and liquids on the ground are טהור. A הלכה למשה מסיני would declare these liquids pure across the board, so the split shows that רבי שמעון is not working from such a tradition.

keyTerms.meaning: the ground or floor
a fixed tradition, here meaning a הלכה למשה מסיני
'What difference is it to me whether X or Y?' This is a formula for arguing that two cases should be treated the same.

phrases.english: And here (Rabban) Shimon says:
phrases.notes: This refers to רבי שמעון's view in the ברייתא quoted in step 1.

phrases.english: in vessels they are impure,
on the ground they are pure.
And if it is a halakha (from Sinai),
what difference is it to me whether in vessels
or what difference whether on the ground?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי הִלְכְתָא הִיא, מָה לִי בְּכֵלִים מָה לִי בְּקַרְקַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבינא's challenge that began in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim (step 2) that רבי שמעון can explain slaughterhouse liquids through a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A Sinai tradition would make the liquids pure no matter where they are. רבי שמעון's split between vessels and ground shows that he does not rely on such a tradition.

steps.title: The challenge remains unanswered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits that רבינא's challenge against רב פפא is not resolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states, in one word, that the question against רב פפא stands and has no answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'קשיא' on its own means the objection is strong and stays unresolved, but it is not a full refutation the way 'תיובתא' is. The idea that רבי שמעון relies on a הלכה למשה מסיני is left weakened.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is difficult.' The question stands unresolved, but it is a softer verdict than a full refutation (תְּיוּבְתָּא).

phrases.english: It is difficult.
phrases.notes: Kept as one word because it is a complete verdict on its own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the verdict on the challenge of steps 5–6.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב פפא's הלכה למשה מסיני explanation does not fit רבי שמעון, and the difficulty is left standing.
steps.whatToRemember: The section ends with 'קשיא': רבי שמעון's split between vessels and ground cannot be explained as a הלכה למשה מסיני.

steps.title: 'Pure on the ground' applies only to water, not blood
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא limits רבי שמעון's ruling. Only water on the slaughterhouse floor stays טהור. Blood on the floor can still become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: What you said, that on the ground they are pure, was taught only about water, but not about blood.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא clarifies how far רבי שמעון's 'pure on the ground' rule reaches. It covers water only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Water lying on the ground has a connection to the purity of a מקוה, which is attached to the ground. Blood has no such connection. So the reason for staying pure applies to water and not to blood.

keyTerms.meaning: 'They taught this only about...' A formula that narrows a ruling.
water
blood

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
That which you said, 'on the ground they are pure'—
they taught this only about water,
but blood, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא דְּאָמְרַתְּ בְּקַרְקַע טְהוֹרִין לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא מַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the difficulty, the גמרא moves on to clarify exactly what רבי שמעון's ruling covers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון's purity for liquids on the ground applies to water only. Blood on the ground can become טמא.

steps.title: Even water must be at least a רביעית
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא adds a second limit. Water on the ground is טהור only if there is a רביעית of it, enough to immerse needles and hooks. Less than that is טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even about water, we said this only when there is a רביעית, which is fit for immersing needles and hooks. But if it is not a רביעית, it is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא narrows the rule even further: only a certain amount of water counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On a Torah level, a רביעית of water gathered in one place can serve to immerse small items like needles, so it has a מקוה-like status and does not become טמא. The חכמים forbade using such small amounts as a מקוה, but they did not extend that decree to the מקדש. Less than a רביעית can never serve as a מקוה, so it is טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: a quarter-log, a small measure of liquid
to immerse something for purification
needles and small hooks, items small enough to be immersed in a רביעית

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean a רביעית is a normal kosher מקוה in practice. It only gives the water a מקוה-like status on a Torah level, which is why it stays pure.

phrases.english: And even water, we did not say this
except when it is a quarter-log,
which is fit to immerse in it
needles and hooks.
But if it is not a quarter-log—
they are impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַיִם נָמֵי לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּהָוֵי רְבִיעִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second limit to רב פפא's first limit in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Water on the ground is טהור only if there is a רביעית of it. Less than a רביעית is טמא.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון, only a רביעית of water on the ground stays טהור. Blood, or less than a רביעית of water, can become טמא.

steps.title: Does רבי יהודה hold that liquids make vessels impure by Torah law?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the ברייתא, where רבי יהודה says 'impure in all cases'. It asks whether this means he holds that liquids passing impurity to vessels is דאורייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: רבי יהודה says, 'Impure in all cases.' Is this to say that רבי יהודה holds that the impurity of liquids, to make vessels impure, is from the Torah?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new discussion about רבי יהודה's view. It quotes his line and sets up a question about what it implies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Treating every doubtful case as טמא, even for vessels, sounds like a Torah-level law. In doubtful cases we are strict only for Torah laws. So the גמרא checks whether רבי יהודה really holds this, and the next part will examine it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Master said.' A formula that brings back a line from an earlier source in order to discuss it.
impure in all cases
'Is this to say...?' A formula that tests a possible implication.
impurity of vessels

phrases.english: The Master said,
Rabbi Yehuda says: impure in all cases.
Is this to say that Rabbi Yehuda holds
that the impurity of liquids, to make vessels impure,
is from the Torah?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּסָבַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה טוּמְאַת מַשְׁקִין לְטַמֵּא טוּמְאַת כֵּלִים דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves רבי שמעון's view behind and turns to a different line in the same ברייתא, רבי יהודה's view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יהודה's 'impure in all cases' means he holds that liquids make vessels impure on a Torah level.

steps.title: A משנה about vessels with an inside and an outside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a challenge by quoting a משנה. For vessels with an inside and an outside, impurity on the inside spreads to the outside, but impurity on the outside does not spread to the inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't we learn in a משנה: All vessels that have an outside and an inside, like pillows, cushions, sacks and leather bags: if the inside became impure, the outside is impure too. If the outside became impure, the inside is not impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge by quoting a משנה. The key part, רבי יהודה's comment, comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some vessels have two usable parts: an inside that holds things and an outside. The משנה rules that impurity can travel from the inside to the outside, but not from the outside to the inside. This one-way rule is the background for רבי יהודה's comment that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn (in a משנה)? An opening that brings a source to challenge something
An outside and an inside of a vessel
Its back, meaning the outside of the vessel
Its inside
Leather sacks used for grain

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in a Mishnah:
phrases.notes: Signals a source brought to challenge what was just suggested.

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַכֵּלִים שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶן אֲחוֹרַיִם וָתוֹךְ,
phrases.english: All vessels that have an outside and an inside,
such as pillows and cushions
and sacks and leather bags,
if its inside became impure, its outside is impure;
if its outside became impure, its inside is not impure.
phrases.notes: Impurity only moves one way: from inside to outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to test the question in Step 10 about רבי יהודה's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רבי יהודה holds liquid impurity for vessels is דאורייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This step only sets up the source. The attack itself comes in Step 13.

steps.title: רבי יהודה limits the משנה to impurity from liquids
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the one-way rule applies only when the impurity came from liquids. If it came from a שרץ, impurity spreads both ways.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: When does this rule apply? When the vessels became impure because of liquids. But if they became impure because of a שרץ, then if the inside became impure the outside is impure, and if the outside became impure the inside is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: This step is still part of the quoted משנה. רבי יהודה adds a limit to the rule, and that limit is what the challenge will be built on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יהודה, the one-way rule is only for impurity that came from liquids. With impurity from a שרץ, which is certainly from the Torah, the whole vessel becomes impure no matter which side was touched. So רבי יהודה treats liquid impurity as a weaker kind of impurity.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case is this said? A phrase that limits an earlier rule
Because of (contact with) liquids
A dead creeping creature, which makes things impure by Torah law

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:
In what case is this said?
When they became impure because of liquids;
but if they became impure because of a creeping creature,
if its inside became impure, its outside is impure;
if its outside became impure, its inside is impure.
phrases.notes: With a שרץ, impurity spreads both ways.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quoted משנה with רבי יהודה's limit on its rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The one-way rule (outside does not make inside impure) applies only to impurity from liquids, not to impurity from a שרץ.

steps.title: Why would רבי יהודה distinguish, if liquid impurity is from the Torah?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the challenge. If רבי יהודה held that liquids make vessels impure by Torah law, he would not treat them differently from a שרץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you think that liquids making vessels impure is דאורייתא, what difference would it make to me whether the vessel became impure from liquids or from a שרץ?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now states the challenge directly. רבי יהודה's distinction in the משנה shows that he sees liquid impurity for vessels as only דרבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים made the one-way rule only for impurity that is דרבנן. It works as a sign that this impurity is weaker, so people will not burn תרומה because of it. Since רבי יהודה applies the rule to liquids but not to a שרץ, he must hold that liquid impurity for vessels is דרבנן. That clashes with his ruling in the ברייתא quoted in Step 10. There, when it is in doubt whether liquids passed on impurity, he rules 'impure in all cases' (לַכֹּל טָמֵא), even for vessels.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it would enter your mind, meaning 'if you were to think'
The impurity of liquids in its power to make vessels impure
From the Torah (not a rabbinic rule)
What difference is it to me?

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge is not saying that רבי יהודה thinks liquids are pure. He agrees they make vessels impure. The question is only whether that impurity is from the Torah or from the רבנן.

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
that the impurity of liquids to make vessels impure is from the Torah,
what difference is it to me if it became impure because of liquids,
or if it became impure because of a creeping creature?
phrases.notes: Both would be Torah-level, so they should have the same rule.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ טוּמְאַת מַשְׁקִין לְטַמֵּא כֵּלִים דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the challenge out of the משנה quoted in Steps 11-12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of the ברייתא (Step 10) in which רבי יהודה treats liquid impurity for vessels as דאורייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה's distinction between liquids and a שרץ only makes sense if liquid impurity for vessels is דרבנן. That contradicts his ruling 'impure in all cases' in the ברייתא.

steps.title: שמואל's answer: רבי יהודה changed his mind
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל answers that רבי יהודה retracted. He came to hold that liquid impurity for vessels is only דרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: רבי יהודה changed his mind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a first answer to the contradiction. רבי יהודה said two different things because he later changed his opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to this answer, the two sources are simply two stages of רבי יהודה's thinking. In the ברייתא he treated liquid impurity as דאורייתא, but in the end he agreed it is only דרבנן, as the משנה shows.

keyTerms.meaning: He went back on his words; he changed his opinion

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Rabbi Yehuda retracted.
phrases.notes: Don't mix up רב יהודה (the אמורא quoting שמואל) with רבי יהודה (the תנא being discussed).

steps.terutzResolutionType: Retraction: the two statements come from different stages of the תנא's opinion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה held, in one consistent view, that liquid impurity for vessels is דאורייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה once held it was דאורייתא but later changed his mind and held it is דרבנן.

steps.title: רבינא's answer: no retraction, two different kinds of liquids
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says רבי יהודה never changed his mind. The משנה deals with liquids made impure by unwashed hands, which is דרבנן. The ברייתא deals with liquids made impure by a שרץ, which is דאורייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Really, he did not change his mind. This one (the משנה) is about liquids that became impure from hands. That one (the ברייתא) is about liquids that became impure from a שרץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different answer. It shows that רבי יהודה's two statements do not actually contradict each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unwashed hands are impure only by rabbinic law, so liquids they touch carry only rabbinic impurity. That is why the one-way rule applies to them in the משנה. Liquids that touched a שרץ carry Torah-level impurity, so in the ברייתא רבי יהודה says they make vessels impure 'in all cases'.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually, used when keeping the original assumption
He did not go back (change his mind)
This one... that one, used to split two sources into different cases
Because of (unwashed) hands, which are impure only by rabbinic law

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to settle רבי יהודה's sources. שמואל says he changed his mind and holds liquid impurity is דרבנן. רבינא says he never changed it: liquids made impure by hands are דרבנן, while liquids made impure by a שרץ make vessels impure by Torah law.
steps.whyThisMatters: רבינא's answer shows that liquid impurity is not one single thing. Its strength depends on what made the liquid impure in the first place.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
Actually, he did not retract;
this (the Mishnah) is about liquids that become impure because of hands.
phrases.notes: Hands are impure only by rabbinic law, so this is a weaker impurity.

phrases.english: That (the baraita) is about liquids that become impure because of a creeping creature.
phrases.notes: Torah-level impurity, so the vessel is impure in all cases.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the retraction answer of Step 14 and offers another way to resolve Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case distinction (אוקימתא): each source deals with a different source of the liquid's impurity.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two statements contradict each other, so רבי יהודה must have changed his mind.
steps.terutzMaskana: No contradiction. Liquids made impure by hands are דרבנן (the one-way rule applies). Liquids made impure by a שרץ make vessels impure by Torah law (impure in all cases).

steps.title: Challenge to רבינא: the משנה would have been worded differently
steps.stepSummary: If רבינא is right, רבי יהודה in the משנה should have contrasted liquids made impure by hands with liquids made impure by a שרץ, instead of contrasting liquids with a שרץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then instead of teaching 'When does this apply? When the vessels became impure from liquids,' the משנה should have drawn the line within the liquids themselves: 'When does this apply? With liquids that became impure from hands. But with liquids that became impure from a שרץ, if the inside became impure, the outside is impure, and if the outside became impure, the inside is impure!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבינא's answer from Step 15. It argues that the wording of רבי יהודה's comment in the משנה does not fit his explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא said the one-way rule is only about liquids made impure by hands, which is דרבנן. If so, the natural contrast would be between two kinds of liquid, those impure from hands and those impure from a שרץ. Instead, the משנה contrasts 'liquids' in general with a שרץ itself. That suggests all liquids are treated as weaker, which goes against רבינא.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (if your explanation is right)
Instead of teaching
Let him draw the distinction within the case itself
Its outside (back) of the vessel
Its inside

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying a שרץ case is wrong. It is saying the משנה should have spoken about liquids touched by a שרץ, not about the שרץ itself.

phrases.english: If so, instead of teaching
"In what case are these words said?
When they became impure due to liquids,"
let him distinguish and teach within the case itself:
In what case are these words said?
With liquids that became impure due to hands.
phrases.notes: Unwashed hands make things impure only by rabbinic law.

phrases.english: But with liquids that became impure due to a creeping creature,
if its inside became impure, its outside is impure,
and if its outside became impure, its inside is impure!

steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's claim that רבי יהודה distinguished between liquids impure from hands and liquids impure from a שרץ.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the real dividing line were between two kinds of liquid, the משנה would have said so directly. It contrasts liquids in general with a שרץ, which implies all liquids are weaker.

steps.title: Back to the first answer: רבי יהודה retracted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops רבינא's answer and concludes that רבי יהודה changed his mind.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is clear as we answered at the start: רבי יהודה retracted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the issue by going back to רב יהודה's answer in the name of שמואל from Step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once רבינא's explanation is rejected, only the retraction answer is left. So רבי יהודה's later view is that liquids make vessels impure only by דרבנן. This conclusion sets up the next question about how far his retraction went.

keyTerms.meaning: It is clear
As we answered at the start
He retracted (changed his mind)

steps.whatToRemember: Final conclusion: רבי יהודה retracted. For vessels, impurity from liquids is only דרבנן in his later view.

phrases.english: Rather, it is clear as we answered at the start:
Rabbi Yehuda retracted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the force of Step 16 and returns to Step 14's answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יהודה retracted. In his later view, liquid impurity for vessels is דרבנן.

steps.title: How far did רבי יהודה retract?
steps.stepSummary: Did רבי יהודה retract only about vessels, still holding like רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון for foods, or did he retract fully like רבי מאיר?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: Was it only regarding vessels that he retracted, while for foods he holds like רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון? Or perhaps he retracted completely and holds like רבי מאיר?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know רבי יהודה retracted, the גמרא asks how far the retraction went.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two other views. רבי יוסי and רבי שמעון hold that liquids make foods impure by Torah law, but not vessels. רבי מאיר holds that liquid impurity has no Torah basis at all. The question is which of these two views רבי יהודה moved to.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them
Foods
Or perhaps
Completely

phrases.english: A question was asked among them:
Was it from vessels that he retracted,
but regarding foods

phrases.aramaic: כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סְבִירָא לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: he holds like Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Shimon?
Or perhaps he retracted completely
to hold like Rabbi Meir?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the conclusion that רבי יהודה retracted and asks about the scope of that retraction.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יהודה's retraction covers foods too, or only vessels.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק brings a proof about a cow that drank purification water
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק begins a proof from a משנה. A cow that drank מי חטאת has impure flesh, and רבי יהודה's opposing view is about to be quoted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Come and hear. A cow that drank מי חטאת, its flesh is impure. רבי יהודה says:
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק begins to answer the question from Step 18 with a משנה. This step is a setup, because רבי יהודה's words come on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion says the swallowed purification water makes the cow's flesh, a food, impure. רבי יהודה's response will show whether he still holds that liquids make foods impure. That will tell us whether he retracted only about vessels or completely.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (a proof follows)
Purification water mixed with the ashes of the red heifer
Its flesh

steps.confusionAlert: The step stops in the middle. Do not read the first opinion as רבי יהודה's view. His opinion begins with 'רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר' and continues on the next amud.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק, תָּא שְׁמַע:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said: Come and hear:
A cow that drank purification water,
its flesh is impure.
Rabbi Yehuda says:

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק, תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a proof to settle the question in Step 18.
steps.raayaObject: Whether רבי יהודה still holds that liquids make foods impure by Torah law.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה about a cow that drank מי חטאת (the proof continues on the next amud).
